title: Sell Mineral Rights in Tunkhannock, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Tunkhannock, PA
metaDescription: Own mineral rights in or near Tunkhannock, the Wyoming County seat? We buy dry-gas Marcellus interests directly and pay cash.
heroLead: Tunkhannock is the kind of small county seat where everybody eventually ends up at the courthouse for something, and for a lot of Wyoming County families over the past fifteen years, that something has been gas.
intro: Tunkhannock is the Wyoming County seat, sitting along the Susquehanna River in the dry-gas Marcellus fairway that stretches across much of northeastern Pennsylvania. Cabot Oil & Gas, now Coterra, and other operators active in neighboring Susquehanna County extended development into Wyoming County as well, and family tracts around Tunkhannock have, in many cases, been pooled into producing units over the years.

Because the recorder of deeds sits right here in town, confirming a chain of title or clearing up an old probate matter tied to a Wyoming County mineral interest tends to move faster than in counties where records are split across multiple locations.

sections.heading: A County Seat Where the Records Are Close at Hand
paragraphs: Because Wyoming County's recorder of deeds and register of wills both sit in Tunkhannock, we can usually confirm title and ownership history for a local interest faster than for families whose land sits in an outlying township or a different county entirely.

sections.heading: Reading a Wyoming County Royalty Statement
paragraphs: If your tract sits within a producing unit, your statement should separate gross value, deductions, and net payment. Pennsylvania's Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act guarantees a one-eighth floor on gross value, but post-production deductions permitted under many leases here, upheld broadly by Kilmer v. Elexco, can still reduce your net check depending on your specific lease terms.

sections.heading: Making the Process Simple
paragraphs: We confirm your deed, check current unit and permit activity, review any statements you have, and give you a clear cash offer. We handle recording directly with the Wyoming County courthouse.

faqs.question: Does being near the courthouse speed up the sale process?
faqs.answer: It often helps with title confirmation since records are close at hand, though overall timing still depends on the complexity of your specific ownership history.

faqs.question: Is Wyoming County part of the same gas play as Susquehanna County?
faqs.answer: Yes, Wyoming County sits within the same dry-gas Marcellus fairway, and several operators active in Susquehanna County have extended development into Wyoming County as well.

faqs.question: My royalty check seems small compared to the reported gas price. Why?
faqs.answer: Post-production deductions for gathering, compression, and transportation are the most common reason. We review your specific lease language to explain what's being deducted.

faqs.question: Can you help me with an old probate matter tied to my mineral interest?
faqs.answer: Yes. Because the register of wills is also located in Tunkhannock, resolving outstanding probate matters here is often more straightforward than in other counties.
